title: Scale AI agents in production
description: Covers Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform architecture across four pillars: Build, Scale, Govern, and Optimize. Introduces the new Agent CLI with automated scaffolding and eval loops, Agent Runtime with subsecond warm starts and 7-day workflows, Memory Bank, and sandboxes. Features production case studies from Comcast (Xfinity Assistant 2.0 with decoupled session architecture) and Palo Alto Networks (autonomous network remediation with 24% autonomous resolution rate).

segments.heading: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: the four pillars
segments.text: Moving from prototype to production requires a vertically integrated stack across four areas: (1) Build: over 200 foundation models, ADK updates, low-code Agent Studio, and the new Agent CLI; (2) Scale: upgraded Agent Runtime supporting 7-day workflows, subsecond warm starts, bidirectional streaming, managed Sessions, Memory Bank, and isolated Sandboxes (code execution with 14-day TTL and Chromium-based computer use); (3) Govern: fleet management via Agent Identity, Agent Gateway, and Agent Registry for up to 3,000 agents per project; (4) Optimize: simulation, automated evaluation, and trajectory observability.

segments.heading: Demo: Agent CLI lifecycle and automated evaluation loop
segments.text: Prototyping is fast, but production iteration cycles often take weeks. The open-source Agent CLI embeds expert ADK knowledge into coding agents (Antigravity IDE, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Claude Code). A demo building a customer support agent for an online shoe store shows the CLI: (1) clarifying intent and requirements, (2) scaffolding ADK codebase, (3) generating synthetic test datasets and executing automated eval loops with self-correcting code updates until all test criteria pass, (4) one-click deployment to Agent Runtime, and (5) running conversational analysis on production BigQuery telemetry.

segments.heading: Comcast case study: Xfinity Assistant 2.0 and decoupled session management
segments.text: Comcast's Xfinity Assistant serves millions of customers across digital apps and hardware. Transitioning from rigid rule-based trees to generative AI (XA 2.0), Comcast solved a critical operational challenge: agent in-memory sessions were lost during rolling code upgrades, causing active users to lose troubleshooting context. Working with Google Cloud, Comcast decoupled session management into a dedicated session service shared across steering, repair, and technician dispatch agents. Live demos show end-to-end technician scheduling and proactive appointment tracking.

segments.heading: Palo Alto Networks case study: autonomous network reasoning ecosystem
segments.text: Palo Alto Networks replaced static support workflows with an autonomous reasoning multi-agent system powered by Gemini 2.5/3.0 Flash, Bigtable, and Vertex AI Search. A Root Agent handles multimodal user inputs (e.g., server rack photos) and applies guardrails with human off-ramps. A specialized RCA Agent executes dynamic investigation DAGs up to three iterations over logs, metrics, and network configs. Production benchmarks achieved: sub-100 second end-to-end resolution, 2-5 second streaming thought latency, and a 24% autonomous resolution rate.
